chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, and Hammad ibn Uthman, and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem with looking at her face and her two wrists when he intends to marry her.
ai.seo_question: What parts of a woman's body can a man look at before marriage in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the specific boundaries of the pre-marital viewing (*nazar al-khitbah*), permitting the gaze at the face and wrists to assess compatibility. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between permissible inspection for marriage and the general rules of *awrah*, emphasizing modesty while allowing necessary familiarity before the contract is finalized.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, and Hammad Bin Usman and Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, all of them,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem with looking at her face and her two wrists when you intend to marry her’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim and Hammad ibn ‘Uthman and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy all have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not unlawful for a man to look at her face and hands to wrists, if he wants to marry her.’”
